# `R CMD check` {.dark-slide background-color="#111C26"}

[BLOCK 5 &middot; PART B]{.eyebrow}

::: {.accent-bar}
:::

[Checking packages against your own R and system libraries.]{.subhead}

## Check on your machine, not CRAN's

`R CMD check` installs the package, checks its metadata, code and
documentation, and runs its examples and tests
([Checking packages](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Checking-packages)).

The question differs by role:

::: {.cards}
::: {.card}
[01]{.num}
[Developer]{.card-title}
"Is my package good enough for CRAN?"
:::
::: {.card}
[02]{.num}
[Administrator]{.card-title}
"Does this package set work **on my machine**, with **my** system
libraries and **my** R build?"
:::
:::

## Running it

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/dl && cd /tmp/dl
R -q -e "download.packages('MASS', destdir='.')"
R CMD check --no-manual MASS_7.3-66.tar.gz
```

## Missing `Suggests` fail the check

```bash
R -q -e "download.packages('R6', destdir='.')"
R CMD check --no-manual R6_2.6.1.tar.gz
```

```text
* checking package dependencies ... ERROR
Packages suggested but not available: 'lobstr', 'testthat'

The suggested packages are required for a complete check.
Checking can be attempted without them by setting the environment
variable _R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_ to a false value.

See section 'The DESCRIPTION file' in the 'Writing R Extensions' manual.
* DONE

Status: 1 ERROR
```

R6's `Suggests` (`lobstr`, `testthat`) are not installed, and `check`
stops. `_R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_` is true by default
([R Internals](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-ints.html#Tools)).

## Skip or install `Suggests`

```bash
# 1. accept an incomplete check
_R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_=false R CMD check --no-manual R6_2.6.1.tar.gz
```

```bash
# 2. install the suggested packages, and get a complete one
R -q -e 'install.packages(c("lobstr", "testthat"))'
R CMD check --no-manual R6_2.6.1.tar.gz
```

::: {.note}
[Which to choose]{.note-label}
For a release, option 2: the tests should actually run. With option 1 the
check runs, but examples and tests that need a missing package can fail
or be skipped.
:::


## Keep the `.Rcheck` directory

```bash
ls R6.Rcheck
```

```text
00_pkg_src  00check.log  00install.out  R6  R6-Ex.R  R6-Ex.Rout  tests
```

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `00check.log` | The full check transcript |
| `00install.out` | Output of the install step, where build errors are |
| `R6-Ex.R`, `R6-Ex.Rout` | The examples, extracted, and their output |
| `tests/` | Test output, including `*.Rout.fail` on failure |
| `R6/` | The package as installed during the check |

::: {.note}
[For a validated environment]{.note-label}
`00check.log` records what was checked, on which R and OS, and the result.
Keep it with the release.
:::

## Useful check flags

| Flag | Use |
|---|---|
| `--as-cran` | Settings similar to CRAN's submission checks |
| `--no-manual` | Do not build the PDF and HTML manuals |
| `--no-build-vignettes` | Do not build vignette outputs |
| `--no-examples`, `--no-tests` | Skip examples, or the `tests/` directory |
| `-o <dir>` | Where to write the `.Rcheck` directory |
| `-l`, `--library=` | Library for the *test installation* of the package |

Dependencies come from the normal library path. To check against a
specific library, set `R_LIBS`
([Checking packages](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Checking-packages)):

```bash
R_LIBS=/opt/rlibs/4.6 R CMD check --no-manual -o /var/log/rcheck \
  xml2_1.6.0.tar.gz
```

## `_R_CHECK_*` environment variables

```bash
_R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_=false  # do not error on missing Suggests
_R_CHECK_TIMINGS_=10            # report timings of 10 s or more
_R_CHECK_INSTALL_DEPENDS_=true  # test-install with only Depends/Imports/LinkingTo
_R_CHECK_SUGGESTS_ONLY_=true    # run examples/tests with only declared
                                # Depends/Imports/Suggests available
```

All are listed in [R Internals](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-ints.html#Tools).

`R CMD check` and `R CMD build` run R with `--vanilla`, so `Renviron.site`,
`Rprofile.site` and the user files are not read. Set variables in the
environment, or in
`~/.R/check.Renviron`; `R_CHECK_ENVIRON` points to a different file
([Checking and building packages](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Checking-and-building-packages)).

```bash
export R_CHECK_ENVIRON=/etc/R/check.Renviron
```

## Cohort testing

Check the whole set you intend to release, together, against a fresh
library. The example uses the repository `/opt/pkgrepo` from the next
section.

```r
work <- "/tmp/cohort"
dir.create(work)
file.copy(Sys.glob("/opt/pkgrepo/src/contrib/*.tar.gz"), work)

options(repos = c(LOCAL = "file:///opt/pkgrepo"))
tools::check_packages_in_dir(work,
  check_args = c("--no-manual", "--no-build-vignettes"),
  Ncpus      = 8)
```

`check_packages_in_dir()` installs what the checks need into
`<dir>/Library`, from `getOption("repos")`, then checks every tarball and
writes the results to `<dir>/Outputs`
([`?check_packages_in_dir`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/tools/html/check_packages_in_dir.html)).
It writes into `dir`, so use a scratch copy, not the repository.

## Reading a cohort result

```r
tools::summarize_check_packages_in_dir_results(work)
tools::check_packages_in_dir_details(work)
tools::check_packages_in_dir_changes(work, old = "/tmp/cohort-2026.06")
```

- **Zero ERRORs.** An ERROR means the package does not work here. Do not
  ship it.
- **Triaged WARNINGs.** Record the decision for each.
- **Changes since last time.** `check_packages_in_dir_changes()` compares
  with a previous run. Keep the previous run.

## Reverse dependency checking

`reverse` also checks the packages that depend on the ones in `dir`. It
finds them in the given repositories, downloads them into `dir`, and
prefixes their results with `rdepends_`
([`?check_packages_in_dir`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/tools/html/check_packages_in_dir.html)).

```r
tools::check_packages_in_dir(work,
  reverse = list(repos = "file:///opt/pkgrepo", which = "most"))
```

For a package on CRAN, [`revdepcheck`](https://github.com/r-lib/revdepcheck)
checks each reverse dependency with the CRAN version and your local version,
and reports the difference.

::: {.note}
[Your repository only]{.note-label}
With `repos` pointing at your repository, only the reverse dependencies in
your set are checked, not every one on CRAN.
:::

## A release procedure

```text
1.  Resolve the requested package list to a versioned set
2.  Download every tarball into a staging repository
3.  write_PACKAGES()
4.  Install the set into a clean, empty library
5.  check_packages_in_dir() over the set
6.  Triage: zero ERRORs, WARNINGs recorded and accepted
7.  Compare with the previous release's results
8.  Promote the staging repository to production
9.  Archive the .Rcheck logs with the release
```

The next section covers steps 1 to 3.
